purpose: cjson is a lightweight C library for parsing and generating JSON.

functions.cJSON_PrintUnformatted: `cJSON_PrintUnformatted` converts a `cJSON` item to compact JSON text with no spaces/newlines, using `print(..., false, ...)`. Use it when you need transfer/storage-friendly output. It returns a newly allocated `char*` or `NULL` on failure.
functions.cJSON_AddRawToObject: Adds a raw JSON fragment to an object under `name`. Use it when `raw` is already valid JSON text and should be inserted without quoting/escaping. Returns the new item on success, `NULL` on failure; on failure it deletes the created item.
functions.cJSON_InsertItemInArray: Inserts `newitem` into `array` at index `which`. Use with a valid array and non-NULL item. If `which<0` or `newitem==NULL`, it returns false. If index is past the end, it appends. It also fails on corrupted array links.
functions.cJSON_IsBool: `cJSON_IsBool` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a boolean (`true` or `false`). Use it on a `cJSON*` to test type safely. It returns `false` for `NULL` and for non-bool items; otherwise `true` if `type` has `cJSON_True` or `cJSON_False`.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToObject: `cJSON_AddItemToObject` adds an existing `cJSON` item into an object under the given key. Use it with a valid object, key string, and item. It returns `cJSON_bool` from the internal add helper; behavior depends on that helper’s success/failure.
functions.cJSON_GetErrorPtr: `cJSON_GetErrorPtr()` is for locating a parse failure. After `cJSON_Parse()` returns `NULL`, it returns a pointer into the input at the error position; on successful parse it should be `0`/`NULL` per the API comment. Use it to inspect nearby text for the syntax issue.
functions.cJSON_CreateObjectReference: Creates a cJSON object wrapper that only references `child` (`cJSON_IsReference` set). Use it when you want `cJSON_Delete` to free the wrapper but not the referenced subtree. Returns `NULL` on allocation failure.
functions.cJSON_SetValuestring: `cJSON_SetValuestring` updates the `valuestring` of a non-reference `cJSON_String`. Use it only on valid string items with non-NULL current/new strings. It returns the stored string on success, `NULL` if type/refs/NULL/corruption, or if overlap is unsafe.
functions.cJSON_CreateNumber:
Creates a new cJSON number item. Use it to build JSON numeric values. It allocates a cJSON node, sets type to `cJSON_Number`, stores the exact `double` in `valuedouble`, and sets `valueint` with saturation to `INT_MAX/INT_MIN` on overflow. Returns `NULL` on allocation failure.
The returned number node is heap-allocated and ownership must belong to exactly one cJSON tree. Do not let a number created directly or indirectly via cJSON_CreateIntArray be shared by multiple parents. If reuse is needed, create a duplicate node rather than attaching the same pointer in two places.
functions.cJSON_IsFalse: `cJSON_IsFalse` checks whether a `cJSON` item is the JSON literal `false`. Use it as a null-safe type test: pass a `cJSON*`, and it returns `false` if the pointer is `NULL` or if the item’s base type isn’t `cJSON_False`; otherwise `true`.
functions.cJSON_IsObject: `cJSON_IsObject` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a JSON object. Use it to type-test nodes before treating them as objects. It returns `false` for `NULL` and for any non-object type; otherwise `true`.
functions.cJSON_AddObjectToObject: Creates a new empty JSON object and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it when you want to build nested objects. On success it returns the new child object; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToArray: `cJSON_AddItemToArray` appends an existing `cJSON` item to an array. Use it with a valid array node and a non-NULL item. It returns `cJSON_bool` success/failure; it’s a thin wrapper over `add_item_to_array`.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromArray: `cJSON_DeleteItemFromArray` removes the item at index `which` from a JSON array and frees it. Use it on a `cJSON` array pointer; if the index is invalid, `cJSON_DetachItemFromArray` returns `NULL`, and `cJSON_Delete(NULL)` is a no-op.
functions.cJSON_CreateBool:
Creates a new cJSON boolean item. Pass a `cJSON_bool`; nonzero becomes `cJSON_True`, zero becomes `cJSON_False`. Returns a newly allocated `cJSON*`, or `NULL` if allocation fails.
No direct misuse here; just ensure the returned node is either inserted into a cJSON tree or deleted exactly once on failure paths to maintain clear ownership.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithLength: `cJSON_ParseWithLength` parses JSON from a non-NUL-terminated buffer of known length. Use it when input may contain embedded NULs or isn’t a C string. It just calls `cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts(value, buffer_length, 0, 0)`; on failure it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateTrue: `cJSON_CreateTrue()` creates a new cJSON item of boolean true. Use it when building JSON trees programmatically. It allocates a node with `cJSON_New_Item(&global_hooks)`; on success sets `type = cJSON_True`, otherwise returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_IsInvalid: `cJSON_IsInvalid` is a type-check helper. Use it to test whether a `cJSON*` item is marked `cJSON_Invalid`. It returns `false` for `NULL`, otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Invalid`.
functions.cJSON_Delete:
`cJSON_Delete` frees a cJSON item and its owned subitems recursively. Use it when you’re done with a parsed/created tree. It walks `next` siblings, frees `child`, `valuestring`, and `string` unless marked `cJSON_IsReference`/`cJSON_StringIsConst`, then frees the item itself.
Call cJSON_Delete exactly once for each owned node/tree. Do not delete a node after passing it to cJSON_ReplaceItemViaPointer when replacement succeeds, because that function already deletes the old item. After deleting or transferring ownership, immediately set the pointer to NULL to avoid accidental reuse.
functions.cJSON_AddArrayToObject: `cJSON_AddArrayToObject` creates a new empty JSON array and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it when you want to attach an array member, then fill that returned array. If insertion fails, it deletes the array and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_Parse: `cJSON_Parse` is a convenience wrapper for `cJSON_ParseWithOpts(value, 0, 0)`. Use it to parse a JSON string into a `cJSON*` tree. On success, free with `cJSON_Delete`; on invalid JSON or parse failure, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_GetNumberValue: `cJSON_GetNumberValue` returns a `double` from a cJSON item only if it is a number. Use it after checking/expecting a numeric item. If `item` is not a number, it returns `NAN`; otherwise it returns `item->valuedouble`.
functions.cJSON_SetNumberHelper: Helper for `cJSON_SetNumberValue`: set a cJSON number’s `valuedouble` and clamped `valueint`. Use only on a valid `cJSON*`. If `object==NULL`, it returns `NAN`. `valueint` is clamped to `INT_MIN/INT_MAX`; otherwise it’s `(int)number`.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInObjectCaseSensitive: Replaces an object member by key using case-sensitive matching. Use with a cJSON object, key string, and new item. Returns true on success; false if object/key/item is invalid or the key isn’t found.
functions.cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive: `cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive` looks up a named child in a JSON object using **case-sensitive** key matching. Use it with an object node and a C string key. It returns the matching `cJSON*`, or `NULL` if `object`/`string` is invalid or no exact-case key exists.
functions.cJSON_CreateIntArray:
Creates a cJSON array from `count` ints in `numbers`. Use with a valid non-NULL array and `count >= 0`; `count` must not exceed the source length. Returns NULL on invalid args or allocation failure; otherwise a new array of number items.
Check the return value for NULL and always destroy the returned array with cJSON_Delete when it is no longer needed. Do not transfer one of its child items into another tree using cJSON_GetArrayItem alone; if ownership must move, first detach the item with cJSON_DetachItemViaPointer/cJSON_DetachItemFromArray, or add a duplicate instead.
functions.cJSON_AddNullToObject: Creates a JSON `null` item and adds it to an object under `name` in one step. Use with a valid object and key. Returns the added item on success, `NULL` on failure; if add fails, the created item is deleted.
functions.cJSON_CreateNull: `cJSON_CreateNull()` allocates a new `cJSON` item and marks it as `cJSON_NULL`. Use it when building a JSON tree and you need a JSON `null` value. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`; otherwise it returns the new item.
functions.cJSON_CreateObject: `cJSON_CreateObject()` allocates a new empty `cJSON` item and marks it as an object (`cJSON_Object`). Use it as the root or a container, then add members with cJSON add-item APIs. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_IsNull: `cJSON_IsNull` checks whether a `cJSON` item is JSON `null`. Use it on a `cJSON*` node. It returns `false` if `item == NULL`; otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_NULL`.
functions.cJSON_malloc: `cJSON_malloc` is a thin wrapper around the allocator set by `cJSON_InitHooks`. Use it when you need cJSON’s configured heap behavior. It simply calls `global_hooks.allocate(size)` and returns that pointer; behavior depends entirely on the installed hook.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts: Parses JSON from a memory buffer of known length. Use `value` + `buffer_length`; optionally get end position via `return_parse_end`. Fails on NULL/zero length or parse errors. `require_null_terminated` controls whether trailing non-NUL data is allowed.
functions.cJSON_GetArrayItem: `cJSON_GetArrayItem` returns the item at a 0-based index from a cJSON array. Use it with a nonnegative index; negative values return `NULL`. If the array is `NULL` or the index is out of range, it also returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_Version: `cJSON_Version()` returns a static, NUL-terminated string with the library version (`major.minor.patch`). Use it read-only; don’t free or modify it. Each call rewrites the same buffer and returns the same pointer.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToObjectCS: `cJSON_AddItemToObjectCS` adds `item` to `object` using a const key string. It marks the key as constant, so cJSON won’t free it. Use only for literals/long-lived strings. Returns `false` on add failure; otherwise `true`.
functions.cJSON_IsString: `cJSON_IsString` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a string. Use it to safely test an item before treating it as a string. It returns `false` for `NULL`, and `true` only when the item’s type is `cJSON_String` (low 8 bits).
functions.cJSON_PrintPreallocated: `cJSON_PrintPreallocated` renders a `cJSON` item into a caller-provided buffer, avoiding internal allocation. Use it with a valid buffer and length; it returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. It fails for `NULL` buffer or negative length, and may need ~5 extra bytes for safety.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemViaPointer:
Replaces `item` in `parent` with `replacement` by pointer, preserving list links and shifting later items right. Use only with valid `parent/item/replacement`; returns false on NULLs, true if `replacement==item`.
Only call this with an item pointer that is currently linked as a direct child of the given parent array/object. Do not pass a node returned by cJSON_DetachItemFromArray, because detached items are no longer owned by that parent. After a successful replacement, treat the old item as freed by cJSON and never access or delete it again.
functions.cJSON_HasObjectItem: `cJSON_HasObjectItem` is a convenience check for object members. Pass a cJSON object and key string; it returns `1` if `cJSON_GetObjectItem(object, string)` finds a match, otherwise `0`. It’s just a presence test, not a value fetch.
functions.cJSON_AddNumberToObject: Adds a numeric child to a JSON object. Use with a valid `cJSON` object and key name; it creates a number item, inserts it, and returns the new item on success. If insertion fails, it deletes the item and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromObjectCaseSensitive: Deletes a case-sensitive object member by key. Use it on a cJSON object and a string key; it detaches the matching item, then frees it with `cJSON_Delete`. If no match is found, nothing is deleted.
functions.cJSON_IsRaw: `cJSON_IsRaw` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a Raw node. Use it to test an item before treating it as raw JSON text. It returns `false` for `NULL`, otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Raw`.
functions.cJSON_GetObjectItem: `cJSON_GetObjectItem` fetches a named member from a JSON object using a case-insensitive match. Pass an object and key string; it returns the matching `cJSON*` or `NULL` if the object/key is invalid or no match exists.
functions.cJSON_Print: `cJSON_Print` renders a `cJSON` value into a newly allocated, pretty-printed JSON text string using the global hooks. Use it to serialize an item for display/storage, then free the returned buffer with the matching allocator. If `item` is `NULL` or allocation fails, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_GetArraySize: Returns the count of elements in a cJSON array/object by walking `array->child` via `next`. Pass a valid `cJSON*`; `NULL` returns 0. Empty containers return 0. Result is `int` and may overflow for very large sizes.
functions.cJSON_free: `cJSON_free` is the library’s deallocation wrapper. Use it to free memory previously allocated by cJSON or by the hooks’ allocator. It simply calls `global_hooks.deallocate(object)`. Passing `NULL` is safe if the underlying deallocator is.
functions.cJSON_GetStringValue: `cJSON_GetStringValue` is a safe accessor for string items. Use it on a `cJSON*` when you expect a JSON string; it returns `item->valuestring`. If `item` is not a string (or is NULL), it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromArray: Detaches the item at index `which` from a cJSON array and returns it. Use with `which >= 0`; it finds the item and removes it from the array without deleting it. If `which < 0`, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddBoolToObject: Creates a JSON boolean item and adds it to an object under `name`. Use it to insert `true`/`false` members. Returns the new item on success, `NULL` if adding fails; on failure the created item is deleted.
functions.cJSON_Duplicate: `cJSON_Duplicate` makes a copy of a `cJSON` item. Pass the source item and `recurse` to control depth: `0` duplicates only the item, `1` also duplicates child items recursively. It returns the duplicated `cJSON*`.
functions.cJSON_Compare: `cJSON_Compare` checks whether two `cJSON` values are equal. Use it on valid `cJSON*` nodes; it returns false if either is `NULL`, types differ, or type is invalid. For objects, `case_sensitive` controls key matching. Identical pointers are equal.
functions.cJSON_CreateDoubleArray: Creates a JSON array from a `double` C array. Use with non-NULL `numbers` and `count >= 0`. Returns NULL on invalid args or allocation failure; on partial failure it deletes the whole array.
functions.cJSON_CreateArray:
Creates a new empty cJSON array node. Use it as the parent for array elements, then add items with cJSON_AddItemToArray. Returns a cJSON* with type set to cJSON_Array, or NULL if allocation fails.
Treat the returned cJSON array as the sole owner of its child nodes. If an element is referenced through cJSON_GetArrayItem, do not insert that same pointer into another object/array unless it has been detached from the original parent. Always call cJSON_Delete on the array root unless ownership of the whole array has been transferred.
functions.cJSON_AddStringToObject: Adds a new JSON string member to an object. Use it with a valid `cJSON` object, key `name`, and C string `string`. On success it returns the created item; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_IsNumber: `cJSON_IsNumber` checks whether a `cJSON*` item is a number node. Use it on a non-NULL item; it returns `false` for `NULL` and for any non-number type, otherwise `true`.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromObject: `cJSON_DetachItemFromObject` finds the first object member by key and detaches it from `object`, returning the removed `cJSON*`. Use it when you want to take ownership of an item without deleting it. If `object`/key is missing, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInObject: `cJSON_ReplaceItemInObject` replaces an object member by key with `newitem`. Use it on a cJSON object and a valid key; it returns `cJSON_bool`. It delegates to the internal replace logic without case-sensitive matching.
functions.cJSON_PrintBuffered: `cJSON_PrintBuffered` renders a cJSON tree to text with a preallocated buffer. Use it when you can guess output size to reduce reallocations. `prebuffer < 0` or alloc/print failure returns `NULL`; `fmt=0` unformatted, `fmt=1` formatted.
functions.cJSON_AddItemReferenceToArray: Adds a reference, not a copy, of `item` to `array`. Use it when reusing an existing cJSON node in another array without altering the original. Returns false if `array` is NULL; otherwise it wraps `item` via `create_reference()` and appends it.
functions.cJSON_CreateStringArray: Creates a JSON array of strings from `strings[0..count-1]`. Use it with a non-NULL string array and `count >= 0`. Returns NULL if args are invalid or any element creation fails; on failure it deletes the partially built array.
functions.cJSON_AddFalseToObject: `cJSON_AddFalseToObject` creates a JSON boolean `false` item and adds it to an object under `name`. Use it like `cJSON_AddFalseToObject(obj, "key")`. On success it returns the new item; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddItemReferenceToObject: Adds a key/value to a JSON object as a **reference** to `item`, not a deep copy. Use it when the same cJSON node should appear in multiple places. Returns false if `object` or `string` is NULL; success depends on `add_item_to_object`/reference creation.
functions.cJSON_IsTrue: `cJSON_IsTrue` checks whether a `cJSON` item is the JSON boolean `true`. Use it on a `cJSON*`; it returns `false` for `NULL` and for any non-true type. It only tests the item’s type tag, not its value.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemViaPointer: Detaches `item` from `parent`’s array/object without deleting it, returning the detached node. Use only with a valid child of `parent`; NULL or non-child items return NULL. It updates sibling links and parent->child, and clears the detached node’s links.
functions.cJSON_CreateFloatArray: Creates a JSON array from a `float` buffer. Use with `numbers != NULL` and `count >= 0`; it converts each float to a JSON number. Returns `NULL` on invalid args or allocation failure, and deletes the partial array if an element creation fails.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromObjectCaseSensitive: Detaches and returns the object member whose key matches `string` case-sensitively. Use it on a JSON object to remove an item without deleting it; ownership is transferred to the caller. If `object`/key is missing or no match, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithOpts: Design: parse JSON from a C string, optionally require a trailing `\0`, and report where parsing stopped. Use `return_parse_end` to get the end/error pointer. If `value==NULL`, returns `NULL`; otherwise it delegates to `cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts` using `strlen(value)+1`.
functions.cJSON_CreateString: Creates a new `cJSON_String` item from a C string, duplicating the input into `valuestring`. Use it to build JSON strings. If allocation or duplication fails, it deletes the item and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateFalse: `cJSON_CreateFalse()` creates a new `cJSON` boolean node representing JSON `false`. Use it when building a JSON tree programmatically. It allocates a new item; on success `type` is set to `cJSON_False`, otherwise it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_IsArray: `cJSON_IsArray` checks whether a `cJSON*` is a JSON array. Use it for type checking before array-specific access. It returns `false` if `item` is `NULL` or if `item->type & 0xFF` is not `cJSON_Array`; otherwise `true`.
functions.cJSON_CreateStringReference: Creates a JSON string node that **references** an existing C string. Use it when the string memory is managed elsewhere. `cJSON_Delete` won’t free `valuestring`. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddTrueToObject: Adds a JSON boolean `true` item to an object under `name`. Use it like `cJSON_AddTrueToObject(obj, "key")`. On success it returns the new item; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_InitHooks: `cJSON_InitHooks` sets cJSON’s global memory hooks. Call it once before using cJSON to replace `malloc/free/realloc`; pass `NULL` to reset to defaults. `realloc` is enabled only when both hooks are the standard `malloc` and `free`; otherwise it stays `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromObject: Deletes the first object member with the given key. Use it on a `cJSON` object and key string; it detaches the matching item and frees it via `cJSON_Delete`. If no match exists, nothing is deleted.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInArray: Replaces the array element at index `which` with `newitem`. Use it on a `cJSON` array; `which` must be >= 0. It delegates to pointer-based replacement, so if the index is invalid or item lookup fails, it returns `false`.
functions.cJSON_CreateRaw: `cJSON_CreateRaw` creates a `cJSON_Raw` item holding a copied raw JSON string. Use it when you want cJSON to store/print preformatted JSON text as-is. If allocation or string copy fails, it returns `NULL` and cleans up.
functions.cJSON_CreateArrayReference: Creates a cJSON array node that **references** an existing child list, without copying it. Use it when you want an array wrapper around already-built items. If allocation fails, returns `NULL`. The child is stored as-is and marked `cJSON_IsReference`.
functions.cJSON_Minify: `cJSON_Minify` is an in-place JSON cleaner: it removes whitespace and C-style comments from a writable `char *`. Pass a mutable buffer, not a string literal. If `json == NULL`, it returns. It scans and compacts the text into the same buffer.
